title: fix(grid): a rowColor row reads in the dark theme and its tint covers the pinned cells
body:
Fixes #12375
Clause-②: no

A grid row coloured by `rowColor` now reads in the dark theme, and the colour covers the whole row: the selection checkbox, the row number, the frozen columns and the right-pinned actions column included. Sticky cells stay opaque in both themes.

## What changed

- **`useRowColor` (`@object-ui/plugin-grid`).** Each of the 23 colour names now resolves to a light and a dark value of one custom property, `--os-row-tint`, plus one surface class that paints it on the row (`bg-[color:var(--os-row-tint)]`). Every class is a complete literal in the source.
  - Light: the same `-100` shade as before (`var(--color-red-100)`), opaque. The light theme looks the same as before.
  - Dark: the surface shade `BADGE_COLOR_MAP` uses for badges: `-950` at 40%, written the way Tailwind compiles `bg-red-950/40`. The six neutral names (`gray`, `grey`, `slate`, `zinc`, `stone`, `neutral`) use `-800` at 50%, like the badges' `gray`, because their `-950` is the dark background colour itself.
  - No value sets a text colour. The row keeps the theme foreground.
  - An authored value that is already a `bg-*` class passes through verbatim, as before. No new refusal.
- **`data-table` (`@object-ui/components`).** The checkbox cell, the row-number cell and every frozen cell keep their opaque `bg-background`. On top of it they now layer the row's tint as a background image (`STICKY_ROW_TINT`). Every row sets `--os-row-tint: transparent` unless its `rowClassName` sets a tint, so an untinted row's sticky cells paint `bg-background` alone, as before. The row also resets the tint while it is hovered or selected. The row's own fill already gave way to the hover and selection fills, so the whole row now changes together.
- **`ObjectGrid`.** The right-pinned body cells (the auto-pinned actions column and author `pinned: 'right'` columns) carry the same literal layer. The header classes are unchanged.

## Why this mechanism (A3)

A sticky cell has to stay opaque, because content scrolls beneath it. The dark tint is translucent (`-950` at 40%). So the cell paints opaque `bg-background` first and then the tint as an image layer on top, which composites exactly as the row's translucent fill does over the table's `bg-background`. The tint reaches the cell through one inherited custom property. That is the smallest carrier that keeps every class a literal and adds no prop. Alternatives I rejected:

- **An opaque dark shade (`dark:bg-red-950`) on the row with `bg-inherit` on the cells.** The cells would inherit the translucent hover and selection fills and become see-through. Also, the neutral names' `-950` is the dark background colour itself, so those tints would vanish.
- **Per-colour descendant variants in the tint class** (a sticky-cell selector inside each colour entry). That would make `plugin-grid` encode `data-table`'s cell markup in 23 places.

## Measured, Chromium 1194, once (one-off harness, not committed)

The actual classes, taken from the changed source and merged by `tailwind-merge` as `cn` does, were compiled with Tailwind 4.3.3 against the shipped theme tokens. The page was a table scrolled so that a black block sat under the sticky cell. I read the pixels in both themes.

| | before, light | before, dark | after, light | after, dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| lowest foreground-to-row contrast over the 23 names | 16.24 (indigo) | **1.03** (light fill under light text) | 16.24 (indigo) | 16.80 (slate) |
| untinted row, for reference | 20.01 | 19.12 | 20.01 | 19.12 |
| sticky cell shows the row's colour | 0 of 23 | 0 of 23 | 22 of 23 exact, 1 off by one level in one channel | all 23 within one level per channel (gradient vs fill rounding) |
| black block shows through a sticky cell | no | no | no | no |

Body text is above WCAG AA (4.5:1) on every tint in both themes. Contrast was also computed analytically from the palette for the muted foreground (the row-number text). Dark: 6.89 or higher on every tint. Light: unchanged by this PR, see the acceptance notes.

## Tests

- New `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/rowColorTint-12375.test.tsx` (74 tests):
  - each of the 23 names resolves to a light value, one dark value, and the surface class;
  - none of them sets a text colour;
  - every emitted token appears verbatim in `useRowColor.ts`, the text Tailwind scans;
  - an authored `bg-red-200` passes through verbatim;
  - through the real `ObjectGrid`, a tinted row's row-number, frozen and right-pinned actions cells layer the tint over `bg-background`, with no other unconditional background colour;
  - an untinted row keeps `--os-row-tint: transparent`;
  - the actions header does not take the row layer.
- New `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/__tests__/data-table-row-tint-sticky-12375.test.tsx`:
  - checkbox, row number, frozen column and right-pinned column are the sticky cells;
  - each carries the layer over an opaque fill;
  - an untinted row stays plain;
  - the hover and selection resets are present;
  - without frozen columns the checkbox and row number are not sticky.
- Spelling updates to existing pins. `gridRowDecorationMembers-8071` and `useRowColor.prototypeGuard` asserted the old `bg-green-100` spelling, and they now assert the colour through `var(--color-green-100)`. Their role, which colour each value resolves to, is unchanged.
- **Ablation**, one-off, via `ablation-replace.mjs`, with mutation and restore proven by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`:
  - removing the layer from the frozen data cell fails 2 tests across both new files;
  - deleting `red`'s dark half fails `red resolves to a light value, a dark value, and the surface that paints them`.

- Pre-tsc battery, each exit 0: `phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `control-bytes`, and also `new-line-citations`. `check:spec-floors` exits 1, the same collapse already on `main` (#12334 remains open, not touched here).

  - the error and warning counts per file equal the same files at the base `96fcf305a`: data-table 1 error and 39 warnings; ObjectGrid 1 error and 215 warnings; `useRowColor.ts` 0 errors and 2 warnings;
  - the two errors are the pre-existing `react-hooks/static-components` hits, outside the edited lines;
  - the new test files have 0 errors and 0 warnings;
  - the population is `**/*.{ts,tsx}` per `eslint.config.js`, which enables no type-aware parsing (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not fixed here)

- **An authored `bg-*` value** colours the row but not its sticky cells. It sets no `--os-row-tint`, and deriving one from it would mean building a class name. The changeset says so. objectui has no dedicated `rowColor` docs page, only property tables, so no docs line was added.
- **Muted text (row numbers) on the light `-100` tints** is analytically 3.86 to 4.43, against 4.75 on an untinted row. This PR does not change it, because the light shade is unchanged. The badge palette's `-50` would raise the minimum to 4.25, still under 4.5. Changing the light look was outside this card.
- **An edited row in the dark theme.** The pending-edit fill `dark:bg-amber-950/20` still outranks a tint in the middle of the row, while the sticky cells show the tint. The tinted-and-pending interplay predates this PR. Carrier: none.
- **Editable frozen cell hover.** It sets a translucent `hover:bg-muted/50`, which predates this PR. The tint layer keeps the cell covered.

## Clause-②

`no`, measured. No export, prop, type member or accept set moves. The one visible contract change: the exported `useRowColor` returns different class strings for the 23 names, and `data-table` now reads the `--os-row-tint` custom property a `rowClassName` may set. Both are recorded in `.changeset/12375-rowcolor-dark-pinned.md` (`patch` for both packages).
